note: D2 release audit (research/d2/AUDIT.md): the split files themselves hold the corpus's registrable domains, real phishing domains among them, so they are not tracked. They are rebuilt deterministically from the corpus recipe (uie.corpus.build_splits); a rebuilt split must match content_sha256 below.

split_random.json.gz.name: random_domain_disjoint
split_random.json.gz.rule: whole registrable domains assigned to partitions; class proportions preserved; fractions={'train': 0.8, 'val': 0.1, 'test': 0.1}

split_temporal.json.gz.name: temporal
split_temporal.json.gz.rule: domains first observed before the cutoff -> train (and stay there, later URLs dropped); domains first observed at or after the cutoff -> eval, so eval contains only genuinely new sites
